---
title: "`ev_validate()` — detect format & canonicalise"
---

## Purpose

Take a differential-abundance table from almost any tool and return a tidy long
tibble with canonical columns, so every downstream stage can assume one schema.

## When to use

The first stage of the pipeline; `enrich_volcano()` calls it for you. Call it
directly to inspect what was detected (`attr(., "ev_source")`) or to debug a
column-detection surprise before plotting.

## How it works

A single detector inspects column patterns and routes to the right adapter.
Twelve input shapes are recognised: **limma**, **proteoDA**, **DESeq2**,
**edgeR**, **MSstats**, **proDA**, **DEqMS**, **MaxQuant**, **Perseus**,
**DEP** (`*_diff`/`*_p.val`/`*_p.adj`), generic **wide-suffix**, and **tidy
long** as the fallback. Wide formats (DEP, Perseus, MaxQuant, wide-suffix) are
pivoted to long first.

Columns are then renamed to the canonical set —
`gene` / `contrast` / `logFC` / `P.Value` / `adj.P.Val` — via an alias table,
with `x`/`y`/`lab` overriding auto-detection. A few format quirks are repaired:
MSstats `log10FC` is rescaled to log2 (`× log2(10)`), and a missing `P.Value`
is derived from a `t`/`df` pair. Finally `ev_apply_uniprot()` maps accessions
to symbols when `species` is given, and the minimum-column assertion guards the
output.

## Parameters & defaults

| Argument | Default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `NULL` | logFC column override; else auto-detect |
| `y` | `NULL` | p-value column override; else auto-detect |
| `lab` | `NULL` | gene-label column override; else auto-detect |
| `uniprot` | `NULL` | accession column; auto-detected when accession-shaped |
| `species` | `NULL` | required only for UniProt input (`human`/`mouse`/`rat`) |

## Literature

No method-specific citation; see [methods](../methods.qmd).

## Example

```r
v <- ev_validate(deseq2_res, species = "human")
attr(v, "ev_source")        # "DESeq2"
head(v[, c("gene", "contrast", "logFC", "P.Value", "adj.P.Val")])
```
